title: Simultaneous acyclic sequences on the Zariski and etale sites
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme proper over a field $k$ [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $m$ have the tensor-pullback section components of [lem-pbc-coherent-etale-comparison-morphism]. For every quasi-coherent $F$ and $n\geq0$ there are quasi-coherent modules $G,Q$ and a short exact sequence $0\to F\to G\to Q\to0$, exact as underlying Zariski abelian sheaves and as lifted etale tensor-section sheaves under $m$, such that $A(G,n+1)=B(G,n+1)=0$. In the notation of the cited node, this is Effaces X m.

source.place: Tags 010S and 010T (universal delta functors), 0BDY Lemma 30.4.3(1) (acyclic embedding), 03P2 and 03FD (cohomology comparison)

proof.text: Properness gives quasi-compactness and an affine diagonal. The finite affine cover construction embeds F into a quasi-coherent module G with vanishing positive module cohomology. Take Q to be the module cokernel; it is quasi-coherent.

Forgetting scalars is exact. The existing flat module pullback exactness theorem gives finite-limit preservation of tensor pullback along etale maps; evaluating the resulting monomorphism on sections preserves injectivity. The sheafified tensor-section functor preserves cokernels, and its natural sheafification isomorphisms identify its maps with m by the component prescription. Hence the etale coefficient sequence is short exact.

Transfer the vanishing on G to large Zariski abelian cohomology through the fixed resolution comparison and change of Ext universe. The etale--Zariski comparison and coefficient-universe comparison transfer the same vanishing to the lifted etale cohomology. This argument covers F=0 and empty X as well.

proof_origin.place: Detailed specialization of the cited effacement and cohomology comparison proofs.

mathlib_searches.query: A normalized morphism from Zariski to etale coherent cohomology extends the identity on sections and commutes with connecting maps; acyclic quasi-coherent embeddings give uniqueness and invertibility
mathlib_searches.results: Eight scheme-normalization declarations, unrelated to cohomology. No match.

mathlib_searches.query: The canonical comparison between Zariski and etale cohomology of quasi coherent modules is the unique morphism of delta functors which is the identity on global sections
mathlib_searches.results: No normalized coherent comparison; library has the generic effaceable delta-functor universal theorem, the acyclic quasi-coherent embedding, and a comparison without a boundary assertion.

Mathlib has no normalized coherent comparison. Source library provides universal delta functors and flat pullback exactness. The existing comparison has naturality and degree-zero normalization but no boundary clause. Its terminal-unit isomorphism lemmas are private.

from.place: Final paragraph: canonical coherent-etale comparison, including its normalization as a morphism of delta functors

lean.statement:
theorem exists_effacing_sequence {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] (m : Maps X)
    (hm : ∀ (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent]
      (φ : F ⟶ G) (U : X.Etale),
      (m F G φ).hom.app (op U) =
        AddCommGrpCat.uliftFunctor.map (((tensorPullback U.hom).map φ).app ⊤))
 :
    Effaces X m
